data.name: Muizz

in_arabic.name: مُعِزّ
in_arabic.meaning: المُعِزّ هو الَّذي يُعِزُّ، المُستَضئِم، المُعَظَّم
in_arabic.long_meaning: المُعِزّ هو الَّذي يُعِزُّ العِبد ويُثني له صَدرَه، ويَنفَعُه وَيُفيدُه، والَّذي يُعِزُّ المُؤمِنين ويَصون مَولايَتَهُم، والَّذي يُعِزُّ العِلم وَيُنصرُه وَيُثني له صَدرَ المُؤمينين، والمُعِزّ هو الَّذي يَستَضِئم بِالرِزق وَيُجير بِالرِزق، والَّذي يُضاعِفُ الرِزق وَيُتَفَضَّل بِهِ، والمُعِزّ هو الَّذي يَمجِدُ المُؤمِنين وَيَجيزُهُم وَيُجير بِهِم، والمُعِزّ هو الَّذي يُعِزُّ المُؤمِنين وَيُحمِدُهُم على المُؤمِنين، والمُعِزّ هو الَّذي يَستَضِئم المُؤمينين وَيُفيدُهُم وَيُجير بِهِم، والمُعِزّ هو الَّذي يَمجِدُ المُؤمينين وَيَمجِدُهُم على المُؤمينين

data.cultural_impact: The name Muizz has historical significance in Islamic history. It was the name of the influential Fatimid caliph, al-Muizz li-Din Allah, who reigned from 953 to 975 AD. He is known for his patronage of Islamic scholarship and the construction of the Al-Azhar Mosque and University, which is considered the center of Islamic learning in the Sunni and Shia worlds. The name Muizz continues to resonate as a symbol of Islamic culture, knowledge, and intellectualism.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Muizz is a reminder of the importance of glorifying Allah, the only source of power and strength. The Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) said, "Allah's Apostle (pbuh) observed the prayers with us and then addressed us, "O people, Blessed is Allah (SubhanAllah) Who has honored us with Islam as a religion, and honored us in the world with sustenance. O Allah, bless us in our religion and our world." (Bukhari) By striving to live up to the name Muizz, we aim to give due recognition and praise to Allah in our actions, words, and hearts.
